V3.summary: Only one Gujarat line verifiably pays for software: the ERP refund (65%, cap Rs 1 lakh; manufacturing MSMEs; GST-registered provider; claim within a year of installation). Official 2022 documents I opened show the ICT refund (65%, cap Rs 5 lakh) covers hardware and cloud-access equipment only, excludes software, and excludes service and trading firms. The 2026 scheme (1 Jun 2026 to 31 May 2031) is known only from press of 9 Oct 2026; the official GR was not found, so 2026 scope for software, service firms and the 85% resident-workforce rule is unconfirmed. No refund line exists for websites, apps, e-commerce or marketing; central Digital MSME could not be shown as live. The refund is paid after the owner pays; the full 65% applies only to bills up to about Rs 1.54 lakh. One Ahmedabad consultancy found, no fees, no ERP uptake data.

findings.topic: Gujarat ICT assistance (Aatmanirbhar Gujarat MSME scheme, GR 5 Oct 2022) - official guideline text
findings.detail: I opened the official draft guideline. It pays 65% of capital expenditure on ICT facilities, maximum Rs 5 lakh in total over the scheme period (up to three applications; operative 5 Oct 2022 to 4 Oct 2027). Covered: equipment for cloud access and networking such as switches, routers, backup devices, servers and computers. The text states that the capital cost does not include the software part of the ICT system, so custom software, ERP licences and websites are NOT paid by this line. Service and trading activities are not eligible. Hardware supplier must be an OEM, authorised distributor or dealer with GST registration; spend must fall within one year before installation; apply on the IFP portal plus hard copy at the District Industries Centre within one year of installation; MSME or DPIIT registration needed. File is labelled Draft; server date 5 May 2023.
findings.date: GR 5 Oct 2022; file dated 5 May 2023; opened 28 Oct 2026

findings.topic: Gujarat ICT claim checklist and application form (2022 scheme)
findings.detail: Official checklist (server date 22 Aug 2023) is titled for the MSME manufacturing sector. It asks for Udyam/IEM/LOI certificate, constitution, a CA certificate on fixed capital investment, a CA-certified expenditure statement, undertaking on other state or central aid, bills, a highlighted bank statement, PAN, GST, last balance sheet or ITR, last electricity bill, GPCB consent if applicable, and a project report on ICT/cloud with benefit analysis. The form (same server date) asks for hardware suppliers and the cloud provider, and the signatory confirms the enterprise has manufacturing activity and accepts recovery of the money if any condition is broken. Shows the paperwork load on a small unit (two CA documents plus a hard copy). Application form: https://msmec.gujarat.gov.in/uploads/pdf/uCIIumrSsli7H9jpsZxXdPb1du1k49sw.pdf

findings.topic: Gujarat MSME Commissionerate scheme page (which refund lines have live forms)
findings.detail: Official page, shown as updated 6 Oct 2026, still presents the 2022 scheme (GR 5 Oct 2022) and hosts forms and checklists for ERP, ICT, quality certification, ZED, patent, technology acquisition, energy and water savings, SME Exchange, power connection, rent, solar interest subsidy, EPF reimbursement, SGST and capital/interest subsidy. There is no item for websites, e-commerce, digital marketing, mobile apps or exhibitions. Applications route through the Investor Facilitation Portal. The 2026 policy is linked from the menu but not covered on the page. Read through a page-reading tool, not by eye.

findings.topic: Gujarat ERP assistance (2022 scheme) - carried from phase 1, not re-opened by me
findings.detail: Phase-1 verifier extracted and read the Draft ERP Guideline: 65% of ERP capital cost, maximum Rs 1 lakh over up to three applications; manufacturing MSMEs only (service and trading excluded) with Udyam or DPIIT registration; ERP should cover production, inventory, sales, purchase, accounting and HR; provider must be an independent software publisher or authorised provider with GST registration; SaaS subscriptions and new modules or users count, hardware does not; apply on IFP plus hard copy within one year of installation; operative to 4 Oct 2027. I confirmed the ERP form and checklist are live on the forms page and that the sibling ICT guideline has the same structure (65%, GST-registered supplier, manufacturing only, one-year filing window).

findings.topic: Gujarat Industrial Policy 2026 MSME assistance scheme - ERP and ICT lines (press only)
findings.detail: DeshGujarat and The Secretariat (both 9 Oct 2026, one government announcement) list ERP at 65% of capital cost, cap Rs 1 lakh, and ICT / Industry 4.0 at 65% of eligible ICT capital expenditure, cap Rs 5 lakh. Period 1 Jun 2026 to 31 May 2031; payments made from 1 Jan 2026 can be considered; components can be combined up to an overall 45% (Category A taluka) or 35% (Category B) of eligible fixed capital investment. Neither article gives a GR number, portal, Udyam rule, or says whether software, cloud or websites fall under ICT or whether service and trading firms qualify; The Secretariat calls manufacturing central. Cloud, other software, website, digital marketing and e-commerce are not mentioned. The official 2026 GR was not found (ic.gujarat.gov.in returned HTTP 500).

findings.topic: Gujarat Industrial Policy 2026 - AI subscription aid
findings.detail: Press says up to 80% of AI subscription fees, capped at Rs 1 lakh a year for three years, for micro enterprises and artisans in thrust sectors (sports equipment, toys, footwear, robots, drones). The Secretariat notes the wording is ambiguous on whether micro enterprises in general qualify or only those in thrust sectors. No official text found; unknown whether a vendor-built automation counts as a subscription. If all micro units qualified it would be a lever for AI automation; on the phase-1 reading it is a tiny segment. Watch item only.

findings.topic: Gujarat Industrial Policy 2026 - 85% Gujarat-resident workforce condition
findings.detail: Both press articles state that enterprises receiving assistance must keep at least 85% of the total workforce and 60% of managerial and supervisory staff as Gujarat residents, presented as a scheme-wide condition with no ERP exemption mentioned. The 2022 ERP and ICT guideline texts read by me and phase 1 contain no such condition. Whether it applies to the ERP line is unknown and could exclude units with migrant labour.

findings.topic: Gujarat Industrial Policy 2026 - quality certification, ZED, technology acquisition and other non-software lines
findings.detail: Quality certification (national and international): 50% of fees and needed testing equipment, cap Rs 10 lakh. ZED (state top-up): up to 50% of the charge left after central aid, cap Rs 50,000 (The Secretariat). Technology acquisition from recognised institutions: 65%, cap Rs 50 lakh (Rs 1 crore in thrust sectors). Patent registration 75%, cap Rs 25 lakh. Capital subsidy up to 35% (Category A) or 25% (B) of eligible fixed capital investment; interest subsidy 7% on term loans for five years. None of these pays for software, websites or marketing; they matter only as conversation openers with manufacturers.

findings.topic: Older Gujarat MSME ERP and ICT lines (Industrial Policy 2020 era)
findings.detail: Invest India's blog on the 2020 policy lists ERP at 65% of cost, cap Rs 1 lakh, and ICT implementation at 65%, cap Rs 5 lakh, under special benefits; it does not define ICT, does not say whether software counts or whether only manufacturers qualify, and gives no dates for the lines. Other marketing aid in that policy is exhibition stall rent (75% up to Rs 2 lakh domestic); no website, e-commerce or digital-marketing line. Implication: the ERP refund has been on offer since 2020, so it is not a new trigger, and I found nobody marketing it. Secondary sources date the 2020 scheme 7 Aug 2020 to 6 Aug 2025 (not verified).

findings.topic: Gujarat quality certification assistance (2022 scheme, ISO consultancy-fee line)
findings.detail: Search-result summary of the Industries Commissionerate page: 50% of certification fees, with ISO consulting fees covered at 50% up to Rs 50,000, overall cap Rs 10 lakh, manufacturing MSMEs only, apply within one year of certification, statutory certifications and renewals excluded. Page not opened by me. Pattern confirms the manufacturing-only design across lines; not a software line.

findings.topic: Gujarat capital and interest subsidy guideline (2022 scheme) - service sector excluded
findings.detail: Search-result summary of the Draft Capital and Interest Subsidy Guideline says service-sector enterprises are not eligible for capital subsidy; operative 5 Oct 2022 to 4 Oct 2027. Page not opened by me. Consistent with the ICT guideline I did open, where service and trading are explicitly excluded.

findings.topic: Digital MSME scheme (central; ICT, cloud and accounting-software support)
findings.detail: NSIC's official Digital Services page lists ERP, accounting, compliance software, cloud (SaaS and PaaS), AI, e-commerce and hardware offered to MSMEs, but mentions no subsidy or reimbursement: MSMEs pay the full price through the MSMEmart portal and NSIC adds a 6% aggregator charge; the only provider listed is Dun & Bradstreet. Page says last updated 6 May 2024 while the footer shows 27 Oct 2026. Secondary sites say Digital MSME once reimbursed up to about Rs 1 lakh and was folded into MSME Champions with NSIC as implementing agency from Nov 2023; I could not confirm it is live, so it should not be used as a selling lever.

findings.topic: MSME TEAM initiative under RAMP (central; ONDC onboarding)
findings.detail: IBEF (12 Aug 2025): the Ministry of MSME will help micro and small enterprises join ONDC through onboarding, digital cataloguing, account management, logistics and packaging help, plus training; target 5 lakh MSEs, 2.5 lakh of them women-owned, tier-II and tier-III cities first. No rupee amounts and no statement that the MSE receives money. A separate Procurement and Marketing Support scheme subsidises MSME Global Mart onboarding (no figures). So the central e-commerce help found is free onboarding support, not a refund for buying a store or website, and it competes with a paid set-up for tiny sellers.

findings.topic: ZED certification (central MSME Sustainable ZED scheme)
findings.detail: Current-affairs summary of a PIB item (5 Aug 2026): as of 31 Jul 2026, 9,83,003 MSMEs registered and 7,03,585 certified; revised ZED 2.0 framework from 18 Sep 2024; 100% subsidy for women-owned MSMEs since 11 Nov 2023. Rates differ by source (80/60/50% by size in older summaries; up to 75% capped at Rs 50,000 in a KNN Aug 2026 summary). A certification subsidy, not for software; useful only as proof that central refund schemes can reach large numbers. Pages not opened.

findings.topic: Central MSME technology-upgrade programme (Budget 2026-27 coverage) and CLCSS
findings.detail: A Mint-sourced pre-Budget report carried by Outlook Business says the MSME ministry was considering a Rs 2,000 crore technology upgrade programme with a 20% capital subsidy for energy-efficient machinery, automation and smart manufacturing for MSMEs with turnover under Rs 50 crore. Described as under discussion; I found no approval and no official notice. It is machinery-focused, not software. The old CLCSS was not checked in this run.

findings.topic: SSIP 2.0 / i-Hub seed support and iCreate Pro-Fund Gateway (startup schemes)
findings.detail: Aggregator listings (Aug 2026): Startup Srujan seed support of about Rs 2.5-10 lakh for student-linked early-stage innovators, and iCreate Pro-Fund Gateway prototype funding up to Rs 30 lakh. These fund the startup itself, not a rebate on buying third-party software, and the SSIP route is tied to students; sources disagree on amounts and I could not open the official i-Hub or iCreate pages. Could let a startup pay for an MVP build, but it is a niche outside owner-led local businesses.

findings.topic: Subsidy-filing consultancy in Ahmedabad (governmentsubsidy.co)
findings.detail: A business page lists the Atma Nirbhar Gujarat Scheme for Assistance to MSMEs among its services next to other Gujarat incentive schemes, with an Ahmedabad (Prahladnagar) address; the page I read is a scheme explainer for the large-industry line, copyright 2024, comment stamp 4 Nov 2024. No fee is shown. So claim-help is sold by at least one firm, but there is no price, volume or client evidence, and no CA or consultant fee for ERP or ICT claims was found.

findings.topic: ISO certification sellers use the state refund as a selling hook (Ahmedabad listing)
findings.detail: Search summary of a commercial ISO-certification page for Ahmedabad (RegisterKaro) says the Industries and Mines Department gives a 50% reimbursement on certification costs; no consultant price was given. Shows the subsidy-as-hook pattern is used for certification, while no ERP vendor using the ERP refund was found in English or Gujarati searches (search tool is US-centred). Page not opened.

findings.topic: Complaint signal: GCCI meeting on access to state incentives (16 Oct 2026)
findings.detail: The Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry met the Industrial Extension Bureau on 16 Oct 2026 to raise practical problems with the new policy, including whether service-sector businesses qualify for industrial incentives, whether NBFC-financed units get capital and power subsidies, whether solar spend counts toward the 50% expansion threshold, and whether exhibition and market-development aid continues. The report mentions no payment delays or claims backlog. It shows eligibility under the 2026 policy, including for service firms, was still being asked about a week ago.

findings.topic: Payment-delay precedent: Surat textile power subsidy (Gujarat Textile Policy 2019)
findings.detail: Apparel Resources (5 Jan 2024): more than 3,800 Surat entrepreneurs whose applications were approved by the District Industries Centre and the District Collector were still waiting for the power subsidy (Rs 3 per unit LT, Rs 2 per unit HT) when the policy deadline of 31 Dec 2023 passed; the Southern Gujarat Chamber wrote to the state to clear the files; no government response reported. Different scheme, department and year, so it is a risk precedent for refund-after-payment hooks, not evidence about the MSME ERP line. No ERP-line complaint was found.

findings.topic: Uptake: Aatmanirbhar Gujarat 2022 scheme overall (carried from phase 1, not re-opened)
findings.detail: Phase-1 verifier read a report of 17 May 2025 (headline: Gujarat disburses Rs 7,864 crore to MSMEs in five years) saying the 2022 scheme paid about Rs 245 crore on more than 2,400 claims. ERP and ICT shares and processing times are not stated. My arithmetic: about Rs 10 lakh per claim on average, so the total is dominated by large capital and interest claims, not Rs 1 lakh ERP claims. My searches for ERP- or ICT-line claim counts (including assembly replies) found nothing.

findings.topic: Pool proxy: Gujarat MSME registrations
findings.detail: Search summary of an IANS item says a Rajya Sabha reply reported 37,56,390 new MSME registrations in Gujarat in the five years from July 2020 and 8,779 closures. All activity types and sizes are mixed; no manufacturing split found, so the eligible ERP segment is NOT sized. Page not opened.

findings.topic: Viksit Gujarat Industrial Policy 2026 - launch and sector focus
findings.detail: Search summaries of Elets and other outlets: launched 15 Jun 2026, effective 1 Jun 2026 for five years, incentives of 15-50% scaled by investment, jobs, technology and location, with a Choose Your Incentive model. Priority sectors named include green energy, auto, semiconductors, capital equipment, textiles, chemicals, agro and food, pharma and recycling; IT and services do not appear in the lists seen, which fits an industrial, manufacturing-led design. Pages not opened.

open_questions_answered.question: Can we sell with 'the state refunds a large part of the cost' as the money lever, and for which segments: manufacturing only, or also service and trading firms?
open_questions_answered.answer: Yes for one segment only: Gujarat manufacturing MSMEs buying an ERP. Refund = 65% of the ERP cost, hard cap Rs 1 lakh, so the full 65% applies only up to a bill of about Rs 1.54 lakh; effective discount is about 33% at Rs 3 lakh and 20% at Rs 5 lakh (my arithmetic). Service and trading firms are explicitly excluded in the 2022 ICT guideline I opened and, per the phase-1 extraction, in the ERP guideline. For the 2026 scheme no official text was found and GCCI was still asking on 16 Oct 2026 whether service-sector firms qualify. Treat as manufacturing-only until the department says otherwise. It cannot be used for clinics, coaching, real estate, retail or traders.

open_questions_answered.question: Does custom software, a website or a mobile app qualify for any refund?
open_questions_answered.answer: ICT line: no for software (the guideline excludes the software part; it pays networking, server, computer and cloud-access equipment) and nothing names websites or apps. ERP line: software cost, installation, annual service fee and SaaS subscription count, hardware does not (phase-1 extraction); it does not say 'custom', it asks for an independent software publisher or authorised provider with GST registration and says the ERP should cover production, inventory, sales, purchase, accounting and HR. IV Infotech's GST status is unconfirmed. Websites, apps, e-commerce and digital marketing: no line on the MSME Commissionerate forms page (6 Oct 2026) or in the 2026 press summaries.

open_questions_answered.question: What are the claim steps, documents and processing time?
open_questions_answered.answer: Refund after payment: the owner pays 100% first. Apply online on the IFP portal and file a hard copy at the District Industries Centre within one year of installation. Documents (ICT checklist; ERP checklist per phase 1 is similar plus a supplier installation certificate and module description): Udyam/IEM/LOI, constitution, CA certificate on fixed capital investment, CA-certified expenditure statement, undertaking on other government aid, bills, highlighted bank statement, PAN, GST, last balance sheet or ITR, electricity bill, project report. No claim-to-payment time is published in anything I read, and I found no measured time for the ERP line.

open_questions_answered.question: Is there evidence of uptake or disbursement for these lines?
open_questions_answered.answer: Whole scheme only: about Rs 245 crore on 2,400+ claims under the 2022 scheme (report of 17 May 2025, carried from phase 1). No ERP- or ICT-line claim counts, amounts or delays found; an assembly-reply search returned nothing. The ERP/ICT lines have existed since the 2020 policy (Invest India, 1 Oct 2020) yet I found no vendor marketing them, which is either white space or low demand and cannot be told apart from desk research.

open_questions_answered.question: Who markets the schemes or files claims for a fee, and at what price?
open_questions_answered.answer: One Ahmedabad consultancy (governmentsubsidy.co) lists the Atma Nirbhar Gujarat MSME scheme among its services; no fee published. No CA or consultant price for ERP/ICT claims found. ISO-certification sellers in Ahmedabad use the 50% state reimbursement as a hook (search summary). No ERP vendor using the ERP refund as a hook was found in English or Gujarati searches; the search tool is US-centred and I did not recheck the Meta Ad Library.

open_questions_answered.question: Are there complaints about the schemes?
open_questions_answered.answer: None specific to the ERP or ICT line. Related: GCCI met the Industrial Extension Bureau on 16 Oct 2026 about practical problems in accessing incentives (service-sector eligibility, NBFC-financed units, solar threshold, market-development aid) - eligibility questions, not payment delays. A payment-delay precedent exists in another Gujarat scheme: more than 3,800 approved Surat textile units were still unpaid on the power subsidy when the Textile Policy 2019 deadline passed (Apparel Resources, 5 Jan 2024).

open_questions_answered.question: Which rulebook governs a new ERP invoice, and does the 85% Gujarat-resident workforce rule apply to the ERP line?
open_questions_answered.answer: Unresolved. The official 2026 GR was not found (ic.gujarat.gov.in returned HTTP 500; the MSME Commissionerate page updated 6 Oct 2026 still shows only the 2022 scheme). Press of 9 Oct 2026 says payments from 1 Jan 2026 count and states the 85% workforce and 60% managerial residency condition for assisted enterprises generally; the 2022 ERP and ICT texts have no such condition. Needs a written answer from the department.

open_questions_answered.question: Is any central scheme live that refunds software, ERP, websites or digital marketing?
open_questions_answered.answer: Not verified as live. Digital MSME (reported cap about Rs 1 lakh) is not shown as a subsidy on NSIC's official Digital Services page: MSMEs pay the full price plus a 6% aggregator charge. RAMP TEAM gives free ONDC onboarding and cataloguing help (target 5 lakh MSEs, IBEF 12 Aug 2025) with no money to the MSE. ZED is a certification subsidy. A Rs 2,000 crore technology-upgrade programme (20% capital subsidy on machinery and automation) was reported as under consideration before Budget 2026-27 and is unconfirmed. CLCSS and PM Vishwakarma-type schemes were not checked.

open_questions_answered.question: Is there any refund for retailers, e-commerce set-up or digital marketing in Gujarat?
open_questions_answered.answer: None found. The Gujarat MSME forms page (6 Oct 2026) has no e-commerce, website, digital-marketing or exhibition item; the 2020 policy summary had exhibition stall-rent aid only; the 2026 press mentions none, and on 16 Oct 2026 GCCI asked whether market-development aid will continue. Trading firms are excluded from the ICT line in the 2022 text. The only central e-commerce help found is free onboarding (TEAM).

open_questions_answered.question: Do startup schemes (iCreate, SSIP) work as a money lever for our services?
open_questions_answered.answer: Not as a buyer rebate. Aggregator listings (Aug 2026) show seed support of about Rs 2.5-10 lakh (SSIP/i-Hub, student-linked) and iCreate prototype funding up to Rs 30 lakh. These fund the startup, which could in principle pay for an MVP, but the segment is student-led startups, not owner-led local businesses, and official pages were not opened.

open_questions_answered.question: Could the AI-subscription aid subsidise our AI automation offer?
open_questions_answered.answer: Only if the line is read broadly and a vendor-built automation counts as a subscription, neither of which is shown. Press (9 Oct 2026) says up to 80% of AI subscription fees, cap Rs 1 lakh a year for three years, for micro enterprises and artisans in thrust sectors (sports equipment, toys, footwear, robots, drones); press wording is ambiguous on whether all micro units qualify. No official text. Watch item.

open_questions_answered.question: Can lines be stacked, and can the refund be claimed in stages for a small first step?
open_questions_answered.answer: 2026 press: components can be combined up to an overall cap of 45% (Category A taluka) or 35% (Category B) of eligible fixed capital investment (50%/45% in thrust sectors); in the 2022 text state plus central aid cannot exceed actual spend. Since ICT excludes software, ERP is the only software-paying line, so there is nothing to stack for us. The ICT text allows up to three applications within its Rs 5 lakh cap and phase 1 reads the same for ERP within Rs 1 lakh; whether staged module delivery counts as 'an ERP' is untested. A Rs 25,000-50,000 first step would refund only about Rs 16,000-32,500 (my arithmetic) even if accepted.

open_questions_answered.question: How big is the eligible segment?
open_questions_answered.answer: Not sized from a source. Proxy only: 37,56,390 new MSME registrations in Gujarat in five years from July 2020, all activity types and sizes (Rajya Sabha reply via IANS, 22 Jul 2025, search summary). No manufacturing split found; the beachhead (wire, cable-harness, electrical and electronic units with 15-100 staff) is a small slice and remains unsized.

verdict_for_candidate.reason: The ERP refund is real and still live (forms page updated 6 Oct 2026; 2026 press repeats the same 65% / Rs 1 lakh), so N2's core money lever stands at the strength phase 1 gave it. But the 'stack' idea fails: the ICT line excludes software, no line refunds websites, apps, e-commerce or marketing, and service and trading firms are excluded in the 2022 rules, so the lever cannot be sold to clinics, coaching, real estate or retail. The lever is also narrow: the refund is capped at Rs 1 lakh, paid only after the owner pays and files CA-certified papers, and has existed since 2020 without any marketer found. Its 2026 scope is unconfirmed: GCCI was still asking eligibility questions on 16 Oct 2026, and a Gujarat textile subsidy sat unpaid for 3,800+ approved units at its Dec 2023 deadline. Net: no score change. Cheapest decisive check: a written answer from the MSME Commissionerate on 2026 ICT software cover, service/trading eligibility, and custom-ERP and module rules.

V3.did_not_work: ic.gujarat.gov.in home page returned HTTP 500, so I could not look for the official Industrial Policy 2026 MSME GR or new guideline files. The 28-page 2022 GR PDF on msmec.gujarat.gov.in is an image-only scan (no text layer) and could not be read; the 2022 scheme terms come from the draft guideline PDFs and forms instead. KNN India page on the 2026 scheme timed out. myScheme pages returned only a JavaScript shell or footer text. I did not re-open the Draft ERP Guideline; ERP rule details are carried from the phase-1 verifier's text extraction. Items marked weak or 'search summary' (ZED figures, Budget 2026-27 coverage, SSIP/iCreate, RegisterKaro, IANS pool figure, Investment Guru uptake figure, Capital/Interest guideline, quality-certification page, Elets) were not opened by me. No consultant or CA fee for ERP/ICT claims, no ERP- or ICT-line uptake or processing-time data, and no official status for Digital MSME or CLCSS were found; the Gujarati-language search returned only an English summary and WebSearch is US-centred, so local-language consultant and vendor content is under-sampled. Not researched: Gujarat IT/ITeS and Textile Policy 2024, PMFME, PM SVANidhi, Export Promotion Mission, tourism incentives, and the Covid-era 'Atmanirbhar Gujarat Sahay' loan scheme (not confirmed as a separate live scheme). About 46 tool calls used.

V2.summary: The official 2026 GR (25 Sep 2026, para 8.1) confirms the ERP refund (65%, cap Rs 1 lakh) to 31 May 2031 for manufacturing, processing and job-work MSMEs of all sizes, with no empanelment rule on the pages I read. Against N2: the claim window is now 6 months after installation (2022 draft: 12); the ERP is described as production, inventory, sales, purchase, accounting and HR, while our demo has purchase and stock done, production partial, and sales, accounting, HR and login missing; the 2026 guideline and forms are not yet published (online forms date from 2023). I found no ERP uptake figure, delay complaint, marketer of the refund, Gujarat price quote or owner voice. The pool cannot be sized from public data; 28 sample units are listed. Verdict: weaker than phase 1; run the written gate first.

findings.topic: 2026 GR confirms the ERP refund line (para 8.1)
findings.detail: Govt of Gujarat, Industries and Mines Dept, GR IMD/WRT/e-file/9/2026/2630/CH dated 25 Sep 2026 (Viksit Gujarat Industrial Policy 2026, scheme for assistance to MSMEs; in force 1 Jun 2026 to 31 May 2031). Para 8.1: aid of 65% of the capital cost of installing an ERP, capped at Rs 1,00,000 over the scheme period. Capital cost means installation, software and annual service cost; hardware excluded; SaaS annual subscription counts. Sanctioning authority in the para 23.2 table is the MSME Commissioner. The PDF is a 32-page scan, so I read it from page images (pages 1-8 and 16-30) and paraphrase it here.

findings.topic: Who qualifies under the 2026 GR
findings.detail: Para 8 opens by saying the manufacturing sector is eligible. Para 1.1 defines an enterprise as a legal entity (company, firm incl. LLP, society, trust, co-operative or proprietorship) engaged in manufacturing, production, processing or job work, so job-work units are inside. Para 1.2 sizes MSMEs by plant-and-machinery investment: micro up to Rs 2.5 crore, small up to Rs 25 crore, medium up to Rs 125 crore, so a 15-100 staff unit qualifies on size. Service and trading are excluded in the 2022 ERP guideline and repeated in 2026 paras 15.4 and 17.2.

findings.topic: Six-month claim window and module list in the 2026 clause
findings.detail: Para 8.1(d): the application must be filed within six months of the ERP installation date (the 2022 draft allowed one year). Para 8.1(a) describes an ERP system with server and software covering production, inventory control, sales, purchase, accounting and HR 'etc.', and the lead-in says 'Next generation ERP related to day to day operations of unit'. 'Next generation' is not defined and nothing says every module is compulsory or only an example.

findings.topic: 2026 GR leaves supplier and process rules to later guidelines
findings.detail: On the pages read, the 2026 ERP clause has no supplier condition (no GST, publisher or empanelment wording), no new-module or three-application wording and no processing time. Para 22.5 lets the MSME Commissioner issue separate implementation guidelines. Para 22.4 makes any breach recoverable with 18% yearly interest. Para 20 says a unit drawing another state-scheme incentive must opt for one (my reading: a unit that already took the Rs 1 lakh under the 2022 scheme may have no fresh headroom). The msmec page for the 2026 policy lists only the GR, no ERP form or guideline.

findings.topic: 2022 draft ERP guideline: definition, modules, supplier
findings.detail: Draft guideline under GR MIS-102022-1271(1)-I(CH) of 5 Oct 2022, operative to 4 Oct 2027 (file labelled Draft, in a 2023 folder). ERP means a fully integrated system on a single database, application and user interface. It 'should' cover production, inventory control, sales, purchase, accounting and HR; installation is verified for network linkage with server and software. The supplier must be an independent software publisher or authorised software provider with GST registration. MSME registration (Ministry of MSME or DPIIT) and manufacturing activity are needed; service and trading are out. No empanelment or approved-vendor list is mentioned.

findings.topic: 2022 draft allows added modules and staged claims
findings.detail: Same guideline: spend on a new module, an added module or new users in an existing ERP is eligible, renewals are not; up to three applications with a combined cap of Rs 1,00,000; payments up to one year before installation count; apply online on the IFP portal plus hard copy within one year. The official form asks for the 'ERP system/module' supplier and features of the module installed. So staged delivery is plausible, but the first install must still be an ERP system, and nothing says a one-module first release qualifies (my reading, untested).

findings.topic: Claim paperwork (20-item checklist) and stale forms
findings.detail: The MSME Commissionerate page hosts the ERP application form and a 20-item checklist: Udyam/IEM/LOI certificate, CA certificate on fixed capital investment, CA-certified expenditure statement, bill, highlighted bank statement, supplier installation certificate, ERP module description, GPCB consent if applicable, shareholding pattern, PAN, cancelled cheque, GST registration, CA-certified balance sheet, latest electricity bill, board resolution. Both PDFs carry a Last-Modified header of 22 Aug 2023 and cite the 2022 GR, so they are old-scheme forms; I found no 2026 ERP form. The owner pays in full first and needs a CA.

findings.topic: No processing time; late-filing and clawback rules
findings.detail: Neither document gives a number of days for sanction or payment. The 2026 GR (paras 21.4 and 21.6) only says applications are to be disposed of within the 'prescribed time limit'. Para 21.2 allows late filing up to two years with a proportionate cut, but it sits in the eligibility-certificate section, so I cannot say it covers ERP claims. Breach allows recovery with 18% interest (para 22.4). No practitioner report on ERP-claim speed was found.

findings.topic: 85% Gujarat-resident workforce condition not found in the ERP line
findings.detail: I found no residency condition in the ERP clause (para 8.1), in the general conditions (paras 20-22) or in the 2022 draft ERP guideline. The 9 Oct 2026 press (opened by the phase-1 verifier, not re-opened by me) states an 85% workforce and 60% managerial-staff residency condition for beneficiaries generally. GR pages 9-15 (capital and interest subsidy, eligibility certificates) and 31-32 were not read, so a scheme-wide clause there is not ruled out.

findings.topic: Other lines in the same GR: ICT and AI subscription
findings.detail: Para 10: 65% of capital spend on ICT equipment, networking and hardware for cloud, Industry 4.0 or AI-related technology, cap Rs 5 lakh, claim within six months of installation, sanctioned by the district GM-DIC. Whether software or an automation build counts is not stated. Para 19.7 (AI subscription, 80% up to Rs 1 lakh a year for 3 years) is limited to micro enterprises and artisans in thrust sectors (sports goods, toys, footwear, robots, drones, others notified), so wire and harness units are outside it.

findings.topic: ERP-line uptake and delay data not found
findings.detail: Three targeted searches by this lens found no ERP claim count, assembly reply, RTI or delay complaint. Only whole-scheme data: the 2022 scheme paid about Rs 245 crore on more than 2,400 claims per a 17 May 2025 report (read by the phase-1 verifier, not re-opened here); the ERP share is unknown.

findings.topic: The refund is an old hook and nobody was found selling it
findings.detail: The same 65% ERP line (cap Rs 1 lakh, hardware excluded) is described in the Gujarat MSME Incentive Policy 2020 text hosted by ICAI's western regional council (search snippet, not opened), in the 2022 scheme and now the 2026 GR, so it has existed about six years. Six English and Gujarati searches by this lens returned only official pages, aggregators (myscheme.gov.in, youthpower.in, publicservicesmap.in) and 2026 press. No ERP vendor, Tally, Zoho or Odoo partner, CA or consultant page selling the refund was found. That can mean unused white space or weak pull; the evidence cannot say which.

findings.topic: ERP price and project-length benchmarks (India-wide vendor blogs)
findings.detail: No Gujarat micro or small unit quote was found. Vendor blogs (search summaries, pages not opened, undated) give: basic web ERP for small shops Rs 50,000-2 lakh; medium manufacturers Rs 2-10 lakh; cloud ERP Rs 5-25 lakh plus subscription; Odoo or ERPNext builds Rs 3-20 lakh; one guide Rs 60,000-20 lakh overall; ERPNext for small firms 6-12 weeks, mid-market 2-4 months. My arithmetic: the refund hits its Rs 1 lakh cap at about Rs 1.54 lakh of eligible spend, so a Rs 1.5 lakh build nets about Rs 52,500 after refund, while a Rs 3 lakh build still costs Rs 2 lakh net.

findings.topic: Vendor case: MySolar, Ahmedabad (Odoo by Softhealer)
findings.detail: Vendor case study (search snippet, page not opened, undated): an Ahmedabad solar balance-of-system maker ran Zoho Books plus separate systems; the vendor says manual processes caused stock mismatches, over-procurement and production delays, and headlines a 30% efficiency gain. A vendor claim, not an owner interview; no mention of the state refund seen.

findings.topic: Vendor case: Florex Green Pipes, Rajkot (Odoo)
findings.detail: Vendor case study (snippet only, undated): a Rajkot PVC pipe maker moved from Excel-based work, where stock was not tracked in a structured system, to Odoo in a stated 4-month project; headline 25% less manual work. It gives one Gujarat project-length data point and a pain description, both written by the vendor.

findings.topic: Job post: Purchase Executive, Vatva GIDC
findings.detail: R.K. Automation Solution (electrical automation) advertised a Purchase Executive in Vatva GIDC, Ahmedabad, at Rs 22,000-30,000 a month, covering RFQs, comparison sheets, inventory coordination and material planning; walk-in window 4-18 Aug 2026 (search summary; page not opened). One post only. Searches for store, planning or purchase roles in Kadi, Kalol, Chhatral, Naroda and Rajkot found no current posts.

findings.topic: No new India MSME ERP-adoption or failure survey found
findings.detail: A search for 2026 surveys on ERP adoption, stock mismatch, late deliveries or costing errors in small Indian factories found none. Results were a 2024 study of 36 South Indian SMEs reporting fewer operational problems after ERP, a 2010 survey of 130 SMEs in one city, and a market forecast (India ERP market about US$1.24 billion in 2026, 16.08% yearly growth, summary of a Mordor report). All are small, old, regional or commercial. The vendor survey and the CII-ISB 21% figure from phase 1 were not re-checked here.

findings.topic: Udyam and GIDC counts are all-sector and cannot size the beachhead
findings.detail: Gujarat added 37,56,390 MSME registrations between 1 Jul 2020 and 15 Jul 2025, with 8,779 closures (Rajya Sabha reply reported by IANS on 22 Jul 2025; snippet only). An undated article puts total registrations at 4,21,026 for Ahmedabad and 1,95,316 for Rajkot (low reliability). GIDC has 248 sanctioned estates, 182 functional, with no per-estate unit counts. No NIC-code, district or staff-band count was found.

findings.topic: Maps sample: reach signals
findings.detail: 32 Google Maps listings from 8 searches (top 4 each) across the four clusters on 28 Oct 2026: 24 show a mobile-format number and 23 a website; 4 look like trading or non-manufacturing and were dropped. Of the 28 kept, 20 show a mobile-format number, 20 a website, 2 only a landline and 6 no number. Three of the 32 numbers share a 9512 prefix and may be forwarding lines (my inference, untested). Owner status and WhatsApp reach are untested; top-ranked listings favour firms with reviews and a web presence.

findings.topic: Our demo against the guideline's module list
findings.detail: Project tracker read 28 Oct 2026. Done: 14 masters; procurement (PO, GRN, inward QC, purchase invoice per GRN, purchase return); inventory (ledger, transfer, adjustment, valuation, opening stock, alerts). Partial: production (order, release, material issue; output, batch, scrap, routing and variance pending). Not started: login and multi-tenancy, finished-goods QC, sales with e-way bill and e-invoice (customer master only), accounting vouchers, GST reporting, expenses and fixed assets, dashboards and approvals, import and opening-balance migration. HR is not in the phase plan at all. Against the six areas: 2 done, 1 partial, 3 missing.

open_questions_answered.question: Who qualifies for the ERP refund (manufacturing only, Udyam, micro, small, medium)?
open_questions_answered.answer: Manufacturing, processing and job-work enterprises only; service and trading are excluded. All three size classes qualify (2026: plant-and-machinery investment up to Rs 2.5, 25 and 125 crore). A Udyam, IEM or LOI registration is needed (checklist). Job work is inside the 2026 definition.

open_questions_answered.question: Does the 85% Gujarat-resident workforce condition apply to the ERP line?
open_questions_answered.answer: Not found in the ERP clause, the GR's general conditions (paras 20-22) or the 2022 draft guideline. The 9 Oct 2026 press states it for beneficiaries generally. GR pages 9-15 and 31-32 were not read, so it is unresolved; ask the Commissionerate.

open_questions_answered.question: What is the exact definition of an ERP and are accounting and HR mandatory or only examples?
open_questions_answered.answer: 2022 draft: a fully integrated system on one database, application and user interface that should cover production, inventory control, sales, purchase, accounting and HR etc. The 2026 GR repeats the list and adds 'next generation' ERP for day-to-day operations. Neither says every module is compulsory and neither says they are only examples; no official clarification was found.

open_questions_answered.question: Does module-by-module delivery count?
open_questions_answered.answer: Unclear. The 2022 draft accepts new modules, added modules and new users in an existing ERP, with up to three applications to Rs 1 lakh, and the form says 'ERP system/module'. But the first install must be an ERP system whose server and software linkage is verified, so a one-module first release is at risk. Needs a written answer.

open_questions_answered.question: What are the supplier conditions (GST, publisher or authorised provider, empanelment)?
open_questions_answered.answer: 2022 draft: independent software publisher or authorised software provider with GST registration, plus a supplier installation certificate. The 2026 GR is silent on the pages read. No empanelment list or approved-vendor list was found in either document or in searches.

open_questions_answered.question: What are the claim steps and documents?
open_questions_answered.answer: 2022 route: online on the IFP portal plus hard copy at the MSME Commissioner's office. 2026 GR: apply within 6 months of installation; sanction by the MSME Commissioner. The 20-item checklist needs CA certificates, a bank-paid bill, the supplier installation certificate, a module description and Udyam. The 2026 form is not yet published.

open_questions_answered.question: What is the processing time from claim to payment?
open_questions_answered.answer: Neither document gives a number of days, and no practitioner report was found.

open_questions_answered.question: Are there disbursement or uptake figures for the ERP line, or complaints about delays?
open_questions_answered.answer: None found. Whole 2022 scheme: about Rs 245 crore on 2,400+ claims (17 May 2025 report, read by the phase-1 verifier). ERP share unknown.

open_questions_answered.question: What must a small custom-ERP builder like IV Infotech have to be a valid supplier?
open_questions_answered.answer: On the documents read: a GST registration and GST invoices; to be the publisher of the software (own code) or an authorised provider of it; a signed installation certificate listing modules and installation date; a live install with server and software linkage an officer can verify; a bank-paid invoice the customer's CA can certify; and in practice the six module areas or a written OK for staged delivery. Not required on the documents: empanelment, turnover, years in business or certification. IV Infotech's GST status is unconfirmed (not in the files searched; ivinfotech.com could not be fetched).

open_questions_answered.question: Who markets or uses the refund?
open_questions_answered.answer: No vendor, partner, CA or consultant selling it and no Gujarat unit that claimed it was found. Gujarat manufacturers do run ERP (vendor cases: MySolar Ahmedabad, Florex Rajkot, Husaingadh), but none of the snippets seen mentions the refund.

open_questions_answered.question: What ERP prices and project lengths are quoted to Gujarat micro and small units?
open_questions_answered.answer: No Gujarat quote found. India-wide vendor blogs: Rs 50,000-2 lakh basic, Rs 2-10 lakh medium manufacturing, 6-12 weeks to 4 months; one Rajkot Odoo case study says 4 months.

open_questions_answered.question: What would a credible first release need?
open_questions_answered.answer: Login and roles; sales with GST invoice (e-way bill later); accounting-lite (ledgers, receipts, payments, GST summary, Tally export); HR-lite (employee master, attendance, leave, payroll sheet); production output, scrap and costing; one database and one screen set; an installation-certificate template; deployment on a server at or for the unit. My estimate: 8-12 weeks of full-time build on top of today's purchase and stock core.

open_questions_answered.question: What should the written gate ask the MSME Commissionerate?
open_questions_answered.answer: (1) Which rulebook and form apply to an ERP installed now, and is a 2026 guideline due. (2) Is a custom ERP from a GST-registered firm that owns the code accepted. (3) Are accounting and HR compulsory; does a staged install qualify and does each stage restart the 6-month clock. (4) Does the 85% resident-workforce rule apply to ERP. (5) Time from complete claim to payment, ERP claims paid so far, common rejections. (6) Does the ICT line (Rs 5 lakh) cover software or automation.

open_questions_answered.question: Is the beachhead pool large enough?
open_questions_answered.answer: Not sizable from public data. My estimate is about 500-2,500 units across the four clusters (low confidence). 28 named sample units are listed.

verdict_for_candidate.reason: Weaker than phase 1 (22 of 35 down to about 18.5), not broken. Confirmed by the official 2026 GR: the ERP line is live to 31 May 2031, covers manufacturing, processing and job-work MSMEs of all three sizes, and shows no empanelment condition on the pages read. Weakened by: (1) the claim window is cut to 6 months after installation (2022 draft: 12); (2) the ERP is described as production, inventory, sales, purchase, accounting and HR, and our demo has 2 of 6 done, production partial, and sales, accounting, HR and login missing, so a first release may not count as an ERP; (3) the 2026 implementation guideline and forms are not published (the MSME Commissioner may issue them, GR para 22.5; the ERP forms online are 2023 files), so supplier rules rest on a 2022 draft needing a GST-registered publisher or authorised provider, and IV Infotech's GST status is unconfirmed; (4) the Rs 1 lakh cap means a Rs 3 lakh build still nets Rs 2 lakh; (5) still no owner voice, no uptake data, nobody found selling the refund in six years, and pain rests on vendor case studies. Next step: a free written gate to the MSME Commissionerate with the six questions in the Q&A list, plus a GST check. N2 stays a candidate only if staged delivery and a custom-built supplier are confirmed in writing; then build login, sales invoice, accounting-lite with Tally export, HR-lite and production output before any factory visit.

V2.did_not_work: The 2026 GR PDF is a 32-page scan with no text layer (WebFetch returned binary). I rendered pages to images with PyMuPDF and read them by eye, so wording is paraphrased and must be checked against the PDF before legal reliance. Read: pages 1-8 and 16-30. Not read: pages 9-15 (capital and interest subsidy, eligibility certificates) and 31-32, so a scheme-wide 85% residency clause is not ruled out. The 2022 main GR and the 38-page general guideline were not read; the ERP guideline is labelled Draft. No 2026 ERP guideline or form exists on the msmec pages I opened; the ERP form and checklist are 2023 files. Nothing found despite targeted searches in English and Gujarati: ERP-line uptake, assembly reply or RTI, claim-delay complaints, any vendor, CA or consultant marketing the refund, Gujarat ERP price quotes, NIC-code or district Udyam counts, and store, planning or purchase job posts in Kadi, Kalol, Chhatral, Naroda and Rajkot. WebSearch is US-centred and returns summaries: the Udyam, GIDC, price, vendor-case and Vatva job-post items were not opened by me. The Maps sample is top-ranked listings only (no Changodar or Naroda results); staff size, ownership and WhatsApp reach are untested and owner-run labels are inferred from names and listing shape. No association directories or IndiaMART pages were opened (budget). ivinfotech.com could not be fetched (connection refused), so IV Infotech's GST registration is unchecked. The B-Square survey and the CII-ISB 21% figure from phase 1 were not re-opened. No owner voice exists and nobody was contacted. About 49 tool calls used, slightly over the 45 budget.

V1.summary: N1 gets slightly weaker, not broken. In 466 of the newest Google reviews of 22 Gujarat solar installers, none clearly complained about a stuck net meter or missing subsidy; the 24 low-star reviews (5%) were mostly about silence after the sale, installation delay and workmanship. Official pressure is real (MNRE 60-day advice, 66 vendors switched off, complaint SOP), but I could not count the Gujarat vendor pool (the portal is script-driven), found no Gujarat job post with portal-chasing duties, and the scheme still ends 31 March 2027 with no notified extension. QuickEstimate and RichAutomate already cover stage tracking and customer messages cheaply. Their public pages show no 30/45/60-day ageing alerts, 8/15-day complaint timers, Gujarati messages or done-for-you list loading, so a thin gap exists. Keep N1 only as a cheap one-week test.

findings.topic: Gujarat Google Maps reviews: what customers complain about (classification)
findings.detail: Apify Google Maps run on 28 Oct 2026: 24 rooftop-solar listings (4 each for Mehsana, Gandhinagar, Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot); 22 returned reviews: 466 newest reviews (344 with text; 403 dated 2025-26). 24 reviews (5.2%) are 3 stars or lower; 12 of 22 installers have at least one. I hand-read all 24. Counts are non-exclusive. Delay or pending net meter / DISCOM inspection: 0 clear, 1 ambiguous. Subsidy not received: 0. No response or no status update: 5 reviews (1.1% of 466; 1.5% of text reviews) at 5 installers (23%); 2025-26 only: 4 reviews at 4 installers (18%). Installation delay after payment: 3 reviews at 3 installers (14%). After-sales or service complaint: 7 reviews (5 explicit, 2 vague) at 5 installers. Other low-star (workmanship, wrong equipment, rude staff, price, one-line insults): 8. No text: 5. Praise: 7 reviews at 6 installers thank the installer for subsidy or net-metering help, all positive; 51 reviews (11%) use communication or guidance words (keyword match, over-counts).

findings.topic: The Maps sample is biased toward big, well-rated firms
findings.detail: 94.8% of the 466 reviews are 4 or 5 stars. Several sampled firms have 500-1,500 reviews (ANK 1,484; Vedanta 1,114; Surya Solar 705; Som Energy 607; Solar Ace 540; Radiant 496), so they are probably larger than owner-run firms under 30 staff (Solar Ace shows 32 staff on a job-board profile). Two listings (Greenpeak Energy, SS Solar System) returned no reviews and three returned only 5. The sample is Google's own ranking of 'rooftop solar installer <city>', not a random draw, and solicited 5-star reviews are common. A stuck customer may also complain to the DISCOM or nowhere, so zero net-meter complaints is weak evidence of low pain, not proof.

findings.topic: Review example: service callback never came (Som Energy Systems, Vadodara)
findings.detail: 1-star review, 17 Sep 2026: the customer asked for service, was promised a call back, then calls went unanswered. The firm replied publicly and cited Tata Power's service policy. Theme: no response / after-sales, not application status.

findings.topic: Review example: no service after installation (ANK Solar Energy, Surat, Gujarati)
findings.detail: 1-star review in Gujarati, 27 Oct 2026: the customer says the firm talked up service while selling, then gave no service or proper answers after installation, and warns others off. Theme: after-sales and no response.

findings.topic: Review example: loan EMI running while system is not signed off (ANK Solar Energy, Surat, Hindi)
findings.detail: 1-star review in Hindi, 27 Oct 2026: the customer calls the team irresponsible and the service bogus. He says he pays the solar-loan EMI and the electricity bill, the earthing was left unfinished, and electricity-board staff visited twice and left. He asks who is responsible. This is the closest review to a stuck inspection or commissioning, but it is ambiguous (workmanship may be the cause) and the only one of its kind among 466.

findings.detail: 1-star review, 20 Jun 2026: the customer says the project was delayed by five months, and also complains about structure quality and engineer behaviour. Theme: installation delay.

findings.topic: Review examples: unfinished installation and no reply (Radiant Solar Solutions, Rajkot)
findings.detail: Two 1-star reviews. 14 Sep 2026 (Gujarati): no service or answer after installation, system off for two months. 3 Sep 2026 (English): installation not complete even after a month, no after-sales service, rude behaviour. Themes: installation delay, no response.

findings.topic: Review example: no paperwork and no replies two months after install (Heliosnatural Renewtech, Gandhinagar)
findings.detail: 2-star review, 19 Jun 2026: two months after the plant was installed the customer still had no receipt or contract details despite calling several times, and the firm stopped picking up calls or replying to messages. Theme: no status, no response. A status message would fit this complaint.

findings.topic: Review example: delay after payment (Solar Ace Energy, Ahmedabad)
findings.detail: 1-star one-line review, 23 Oct 2026: bad experience after payment, installation delayed. No detail on net meter or subsidy.

findings.topic: Review example (praise): subsidy and net-metering steps explained (Ample Solar, Gandhinagar)
findings.detail: 5-star review, 3 Aug 2026: the team was professional, finished on time and explained the whole process clearly, including the subsidy and net-metering steps. Shows customers notice and reward process communication, and that some installers already do it without a tool.

findings.topic: Review example (praise): support until the subsidy arrives (Surya Solar And Waters, Ahmedabad)
findings.detail: 5-star review, 27 Apr 2026: clear pricing, good materials and service until the subsidy was received. A second 5-star review (3 May 2026) praises help from planning to getting the government subsidy.

findings.topic: Review example (praise): subsidy received in 45 days (Heliosnatural Renewtech, Gandhinagar)
findings.detail: 5-star review, 29 Apr 2025: fast installation and honest guidance; the customer says the subsidy arrived within 45 days thanks to a smooth online portal. A Gujarat data point against 'subsidy is always stuck'.

findings.topic: Public complaint on X: another state, none found for Gujarat
findings.detail: A public X post (Nov 2025) from an Odisha applicant lays out dates: panels installed 14 Oct 2025, new meter 17 Oct, and more than a month later still no installation status update and no subsidy. It shows the stuck-with-no-status complaint exists on the portal side, but it is one post, from Odisha, not about an installer. No equivalent Gujarat post turned up in X, Reddit or Gujarati searches.
findings.date: 2025-11 (post refers to events 12 Sep to 29 Oct 2025)

findings.topic: Gujarat regulator considered waiving the formal net-metering agreement for residential PM Surya Ghar users
findings.detail: SolarQuarter reported a GERC hearing on a Gujarat DISCOM petition to exempt residential PM Surya Ghar consumers from signing a formal net-metering agreement. I saw this only in a search summary and found no outcome. It shows Gujarat DISCOMs were trying to remove a paperwork step, which may reduce the stuck-application problem.

findings.topic: Gujarat scale and the application pipeline (arithmetic added)
findings.detail: IANS 4 Jun 2026 (opened twice in phase 1): May 2026 campaign month had 3,06,230 applications, 35,311 installations, 42,554 DISCOM inspections and 210 new vendors; cumulative over 10.66 lakh applications and 6.81 lakh installations. My arithmetic: 3.85 lakh applications (36%) are not yet installed, an upper bound for the live backlog because it includes drop-outs. In May alone applications were 8.7 times installations. A big pipeline exists, but the source does not say how much of it is stuck.

findings.topic: Gujarat monthly installation run-rate (my estimate)
findings.detail: My estimate: about 21,800 Gujarat installations a month. Method: (6.81 lakh at end May 2026, IANS, minus 281,769 on 21 Nov 2024, a Lok Sabha figure that I saw only in a search summary of a newsonair report) divided by 18.3 months. May 2026 was a campaign month at 35,311. At 21,800 to 35,300 a month, roughly 110,000 to 180,000 more Gujarat installations fall before 31 Mar 2027 (5.1 months left). The Nov 2024 baseline was not opened.

findings.topic: Official scheme end date: 31 March 2027
findings.detail: Cabinet approved PM Surya Ghar on 29 Feb 2024 (outlay Rs 75,021 crore, implementation to FY 2026-27). MNRE operational guidelines of June 2024 state implementation continues until 31 Mar 2027. Seen through search summaries of powerline.net.in and indianinfrastructure.com (both 21 Jun 2024), not opened. Consistent with the phase-1 finding that the 27 Aug 2026 article says under nine months remained. About 5 months of the busy period are left.

findings.topic: Extension and successor scheme: talk only, nothing notified
findings.detail: An installer-blog roundup found no official extension or successor notification as of 14 Oct 2026. An EQ report (cited by an installer blog as 5 Sep 2026; not opened) says the Centre is weighing a 3-4 month extension and consulting on a successor. 'PM Surya Ghar 2.0' is an unofficial label. Installer blogs are already marketing a last-date rush (17 Oct 2026). What happens to unfinished applications after March 2027 was not found.

findings.topic: Gujarat vendor count: no official figure; sources conflict
findings.detail: No official Gujarat vendor count obtained. Phase-1 found 'over 1,100' Gujarat solar vendors (GUVNL MD, 14 Feb 2025, whole ecosystem) and 210 new Gujarat scheme vendors in May 2026 alone (IANS). A vendor blog (updated 14 Jul 2026) says about 70,000-75,000 EPCs are registered nationally (attributed to MNRE) and about 25,000-30,000 are active, with Gujarat holding 22-25% of active EPCs (unsourced). My arithmetic on those unsourced numbers gives about 5,500-7,500 active Gujarat EPCs, which conflicts with the 1,100 figure. Another vendor post cites 26,000+ empanelled vendors nationally in Mar 2026. Definitions (registered, empanelled, active) differ.

findings.topic: The 66 deactivated vendors: no public name list or state breakdown found
findings.detail: SolarQuarter (27 Aug 2026), Mercom, Energetica, Indian PSU and PowerPeak coverage surfaced no names, states or any Gujarat firm. MNRE notice dated 24 Aug 2026: deactivated vendors cannot take new applications and disappear from the consumer vendor-selection page, keep portal access to finish existing work, and get 30 days to cut backlog. The trigger was applications stuck at 'Agreement Uploaded' above installation capacity. The 60-day advice applies to all vendors and is advisory; no built-in portal alert was confirmed. The complaint SOP says names of deactivated vendors will be shown on the national portal, which I could not read, so whether a Gujarat firm is included is unknown.

findings.topic: QuickEstimate CRM: stage tracking and pricing already on sale
findings.detail: Page read 28 Oct 2026 (undated vendor page). Seven stages including a DISCOM net-metering stage (application, feasibility, meter) and a PM Surya Ghar subsidy-application stage, WhatsApp follow-up reminders and WhatsApp proposal sending. Plans: Free Rs 0 (1 user, 10 proposals a month, watermark); Pro Rs 6,999 per user per year with a 3-user minimum (at least about Rs 20,997 a year, my arithmetic) including WhatsApp Business; Enterprise for 25+ users. A vendor price claim, not an observed purchase.

findings.topic: QuickEstimate CRM: what the page does not show
findings.detail: The same page does not mention ageing alerts at 30, 45 or 60 days, complaint timers, customer-facing status-update messages, Gujarati or Hindi support, or any data-import tool or done-for-you onboarding. It says moving historical leads from a spreadsheet takes longer and is best done after new leads are running. Absence from a public page is not proof the product lacks it.

findings.topic: RichAutomate: customer-facing DISCOM and PM Surya Ghar status messages, zero setup
findings.detail: Vendor blog dated 5 Aug 2026. WhatsApp API platform for solar EPCs that pushes DISCOM net-metering stages (application submitted, feasibility cleared, meter scheduled, meter installed) and PM Surya Ghar stages (registered, feasibility approved, installed, inspection done, subsidy released) into the customer thread, with document checklists and reminders. Rs 0 platform fee, Rs 0 setup, Rs 0 monthly minimum; Rs 0.10 per message plus Meta fee (Client Pay) or Rs 1.50 marketing / Rs 0.50 utility per conversation (SaaS Pay); 14-day trial. Free done-for-you migration is offered to customers switching providers. No Gujarati or Hindi, no ageing alerts, no complaint timers, no installer-pain statistics on the page. It says the automation never files the claim.

findings.topic: SunbaseData: evidence inconsistent, treat as unverified
findings.detail: A search snippet describes a SunbaseData post with a 12-stage PM Surya Ghar pipeline, but the fetched blog text had no India or PM Surya Ghar content, no ageing alerts or complaint timers, no WhatsApp status messaging, and quoted plans from US$59 per user per month. The two readings conflict, so I do not rely on SunbaseData either way.

findings.topic: DISCOM approval times and installer cost illustration (vendor estimates)
findings.detail: QuickEstimate Gujarat page (updated 14 Jul 2026) gives uncited average approval times: DGVCL 45-75 days, UGVCL 30-60, MGVCL 45-90, PGVCL 30-75, overall 30-90 days to active net metering. Its trends page says PGVCL/UGVCL feasibility averaged 11 days in Q1 and 9 days in Q2 2026 (vendor's own review). Gujarat installer blogs (Heaven Green Energy, search summary) give end-to-end timelines of 45-75 days. The page also illustrates a 12-person Surat EPC spending Rs 80,000 a month on four field reps at Rs 20,000 and Rs 35,000 on marketing, labelled illustrative. No Gujarat vendor counts or tracking practice on the page.

findings.topic: Job posts: liaison roles exist, but no Gujarat post with portal-chasing duties or pay verified
findings.detail: Opened three Weekday pages. Solar Ace (Ahmedabad HQ, 32 staff per the page) lists a Liaisoning Executive Solar EPC in Pune with no duties or pay. Shubham Solar Solution lists an Executive Liaison with no city, duties or pay. Bushnell Technik's Solar Liaison Executive is in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh with no duties (a search summary saying Ahmedabad and UGVCL was wrong). A Hyderabad liaison role mentioning PM Surya Ghar subsidy documentation and Rs 13,000-25,000 a month appears only in a search snippet, not opened. Phase 1 also has a Surat service-coordinator post at Rs 17,000-25,000 (inverter service, not application chasing).

findings.topic: Free-to-join installer lead marketplace and free vendor registration
findings.detail: SolarCalculators.in guide dated 5 Jun 2026 (a lead-generation site, vendor claims): vendor registration on the portal is free; needs GST, business registration, electrical contractor licence, PAN, bank proof and at least one commissioned project; verification 7-21 working days; subsidy typically 30-90 days after commissioning, with Gujarat and Rajasthan called faster states. The site invites installers to join its lead marketplace free. Free lead and registration routes lower what installers expect to pay for tools, and fast Gujarat disbursal would reduce pain.

findings.topic: How installers handle the portal today: indirect hints only
findings.detail: No direct evidence of Excel or WhatsApp-group practice, or of CSC operator or outsourced data-entry prices. Indirect: a Uttar Pradesh / Uttarakhand installer FAQ advertises handling the portal end to end including subsidy tracking (undated); an Andhra Pradesh installer blog admits some installers fail to update installation progress on the portal (undated); blogs say the consumer portal shows milestone statuses and sends an application reference by SMS. So customers can already see some status, and installers sell portal handling as part of the service.

findings.topic: No tool with 60-day ageing alerts or backlog tracking found
findings.detail: A search for dashboards, alerts or export tools for PM Surya Ghar pending applications or the 60-day advice returned only news on the 66-vendor action; none of the five outlets mention a tool. Together with the missing features on the QuickEstimate and RichAutomate pages, the specific 30/45/60-day and 8/15-day timers look unserved in public view. This is absence of evidence from a limited search.

open_questions_answered.question: (1) Do Gujarat households complain that installers do not update them, or that the net meter, inspection or subsidy is stuck?
open_questions_answered.answer: Barely, and not about net meter or subsidy. Of 466 recent reviews of 22 installers, 0 clearly complained about a pending net meter, inspection or missing subsidy (1 ambiguous Hindi review mentions electricity-board staff visiting twice). 5 reviews at 5 installers (4 in 2025-26) say calls or messages went unanswered; 3 reviews at 3 installers cite installation delay after payment; 7 reviews at 5 installers cite poor after-sales service. 7 reviews at 6 installers thank the installer for subsidy or net-metering help, all positive, one saying subsidy came in 45 days. The sample is biased toward large, highly rated firms, so micro-installers are under-represented.

open_questions_answered.question: Review shares and installers affected
open_questions_answered.answer: 3 stars or lower: 24 of 466 reviews (5.2%; 20 of 403 in 2025-26 = 5.0%); 12 of 22 installers have at least one. No response or no update: 1.1% of reviews, 5 installers (23%). Installation delay: 0.6%, 3 installers (14%). After-sales or service: 1.5%, 5 installers (23%). Net-meter or inspection delay: 0%. Subsidy not received: 0%. Praise using communication or guidance words: about 11% (keyword match, over-counts).

open_questions_answered.question: Public complaint threads (X, Reddit, YouTube, news) about PM Surya Ghar delays in Gujarat
open_questions_answered.answer: None found for Gujarat. One public X post is from Odisha (subsidy and status stuck for over a month). Reddit could not be reached (search tool blocks it; an Apify query returned installer blogs). YouTube comments and Facebook groups were not tried. A Gujarati-language search returned only US pages. The only complaint articles known are national 2024 Mercom pieces from phase 1 (paywalled, not re-opened).

open_questions_answered.question: (2) How many Gujarat vendors are on the PM Surya Ghar portal, by DISCOM or district?
open_questions_answered.answer: Not obtained. The official portal returned a blank script shell (HTTP 200, no content) and I used no logins or sign-ups. Bounds from other sources: over 1,100 Gujarat solar vendors (GUVNL MD, Feb 2025, whole ecosystem); 210 new scheme vendors in May 2026 alone (IANS); a vendor blog implies about 5,500-7,500 active Gujarat EPCs (my arithmetic on unsourced numbers, conflicts with the first). No split by UGVCL or district exists in anything I could open. My estimate for planning: low thousands, unverified, until someone reads the portal list in a normal browser.

open_questions_answered.question: What share of vendors look owner-run and small, and are they reachable?
open_questions_answered.answer: Cannot be determined from Maps or the portal. In the 24-firm sample, 6 have 450+ reviews and one (Solar Ace) shows 32 staff, so many are probably above the owner-run size. A vendor claims only about 40% of registered EPCs nationally are active (unsourced). Reach: 22 of 24 Maps listings publish a mobile-format number, 1 a landline, 1 none; whether the number reaches the owner's WhatsApp is untested.

open_questions_answered.question: Was any Gujarat vendor among the 66 deactivated in August 2026 or later, and are those lists public?
open_questions_answered.answer: Unknown. No outlet I surfaced printed the 66 names or their states. The complaint SOP says names of deactivated vendors will be displayed on the national portal, so a public list probably exists there but I could not read it. No vendor deactivated under the complaint SOP was found either.

open_questions_answered.question: (3) Which gap features exist in solar CRMs and WhatsApp tools for Indian EPCs: 30/45/60-day ageing alerts, 8/15-day complaint timers, Gujarati customer status messages, done-for-you loading of the installer's own list?
open_questions_answered.answer: On public pages: ageing alerts at 30/45/60 days: none seen (QuickEstimate, RichAutomate, SunbaseData). Complaint timers at 8/15 days: none seen. Customer-facing stage messages: RichAutomate yes (English page, DISCOM and PM Surya Ghar stages); QuickEstimate sends proposals and follow-up reminders but no status messages shown. Gujarati or Hindi: not mentioned anywhere. Done-for-you list loading: QuickEstimate offers none (says spreadsheet import takes longer); RichAutomate offers free migration only to customers switching providers. So the gap is real on paper but small in feature terms, and a rival could add it in weeks.

open_questions_answered.question: What could a done-for-you service add beyond those tools?
open_questions_answered.answer: My inference: (a) load the installer's own pending list and keep it current, since no page offers this; (b) an 'Agreement Uploaded over 60 days' count that matches the exact metric MNRE used on 27 Aug 2026, plus 8/15-day clocks for any consumer complaint matching the 22 Jun 2026 SOP; (c) Gujarati customer status messages and a weekly human-checked 'who to call today' list. Risks: stage data still has to be typed in or exported from the portal (export ability not checked), and WhatsApp status messaging alone is a commodity at Rs 0 setup.

open_questions_answered.question: (4) How do installers track applications today, and what does that cost?
open_questions_answered.answer: Not observed. No Excel, WhatsApp-group or CSC-operator evidence, and no price for outsourced portal data entry, was found. Hints: the consumer portal shows milestone statuses (blog claim); installers advertise handling the portal and subsidy tracking for the customer; one vendor illustrates a 12-person Surat EPC paying four field reps Rs 20,000 each a month (vendor-authored illustration, not a survey).

open_questions_answered.question: (5) Scheme end date, extension, Gujarat run-rate, and demand after March 2027
open_questions_answered.answer: End date is 31 Mar 2027 (MNRE guidelines, Cabinet approval Feb 2024). No extension or successor notified as of mid-Oct 2026; a 3-4 month extension and a successor are reported as under consideration (EQ report, not opened). Gujarat run-rate: my estimate about 21,800 installations a month over the last 18 months, 35,311 in the May 2026 campaign month, implying roughly 110,000-180,000 more installs before the deadline. After March 2027: not found; my expectation is a drop in new central-subsidy applications and a tail of unfinished applications, with no evidence either way on a Gujarat state top-up.

open_questions_answered.question: (6) Do small installers pay for tools, staff or lead services?
open_questions_answered.answer: Prices exist but purchases were not observed: QuickEstimate Free and Pro Rs 6,999 per user per year (3-user minimum); SurgePV Rs 500-1,500 per user per month (phase-1 vendor claim); RichAutomate per-message fees; lead marketplaces advertise free joining; vendor registration is free. Staff: liaison roles exist (Solar Ace, a 32-person Ahmedabad firm, advertises one in Pune; Surat service coordinator Rs 17,000-25,000 from phase 1; Hyderabad liaison Rs 13,000-25,000 from a search snippet). No Gujarat post with application-chasing duties and pay was verified, and no installer was seen buying a status tool.

open_questions_answered.question: Public job posts for solar liaison, documentation or portal-coordinator roles in Gujarat
open_questions_answered.answer: None verified with duties and pay. The three pages opened carry no duties or pay (Solar Ace in Pune, Shubham Solar Solution with no city, Bushnell Technik in Aligarh Uttar Pradesh). Indeed, Naukri, WorkIndia and Apna were not queried directly. A Surat liaison post with 'Rs 25k+' appeared in a search snippet only (page was a 404 in phase 1).
