verdict_for_candidate.reason: Confirms: the pressure is official and current (complaint SOP 22 Jun 2026, 66 vendors switched off, 60-day advice to all vendors), Gujarat volume is huge with a large application pipeline, and the public pages of the two closest tools show no 30/45/60-day ageing alerts, 8/15-day complaint timers, Gujarati status messages or done-for-you list loading. Refutes or fails to support: no clear net-meter or subsidy complaint in 466 Gujarat reviews (5% low-star, mostly silence after sale, installation delay, workmanship); no Gujarat job post with portal-chasing duties verified; the vendor pool is uncounted (1,100+ to a claimed 5,500+); stage tracking and customer WhatsApp messages are already sold at Rs 0 to Rs 6,999 per user per year or per message; the scheme ends 31 Mar 2027 with no notified extension. The gap is a few features a rival can add in weeks, so N1 rests on owners paying for done-for-you service, which nobody has tested. Keep it only as the cheap one-week test, led by a free 'applications over 60 days' report, and read the portal vendor list in a normal browser first.

V1.did_not_work: Official PM Surya Ghar portal: Apify web-fetch of pmsuryaghar.gov.in took 162 s and returned HTTP 200 with empty content (script-driven app), so no vendor list, no Gujarat or UGVCL count, no deactivated-vendor names; no logins or sign-ups attempted. GEDA / solarrooftop.gujarat.gov.in roster: searches surfaced no public list. Reddit: the search tool blocks reddit.com and an Apify web-browser query returned installer blogs, not threads, so no Reddit data; YouTube comments and Facebook groups not tried. Gujarati-language news search returned only US pages. SunbaseData blog: fetched text had no India content, inconsistent with a search snippet; unverified. Job boards: Indeed, Naukri, WorkIndia and Apna not queried directly; the three Weekday pages opened carry no duties or pay, and Bushnell Technik is in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, not Ahmedabad as a search summary claimed; a Surat climatechangejobs post was a 404 in phase 1. Not found: installers' Excel or WhatsApp practice, CSC or outsourced portal data-entry prices. End-date and extension evidence comes from search summaries (PIB, MNRE pages and the EQ report not opened); the 21 Nov 2024 Gujarat baseline (281,769) is also from a search summary. Maps sample: top-ranked, mostly large, highly rated firms; newest 25 reviews each; all 24 low-star reviews hand-read but 4-5 star reviews only keyword-scanned; some Gujarati and Hindi text auto-translated; reviewer names excluded by design. About 51 tool calls used against a budget of about 45; Apify spend roughly US$0.40 (my estimate from per-event prices).

V4.summary: Coverage sweep A, about 49 tool calls. Nothing in these four sectors beats N1 or N2 (22 of 35). No sector gave an owner-voice complaint, a public Gujarat back-office job post, or an owner buying software for the problem; the evidence is regulatory and enforcement news plus vendor pages. Two candidates have real but weak-fit evidence. (1) Gujarat plastic-waste recyclers registered on the CPCB EPR portal: best-dated chain (MoEFCC notice 28 Aug 2026; CPCB direction of 26 Jun 2026 to states; NGT order of 27 Mar 2026) and a counted pool (662 in Gujarat, reported 7 Jul 2026), but no recycler voice and no software spend; about 21 of 35 on the phase-1 rubric (my estimate, unvalidated). (2) Gujarat fertiliser, pesticide and seed dealers under PoS-versus-stock inspections: good official 2026 numbers but cheap software already exists (about Rs 9,500); about 19 of 35 (my estimate). Auto belts are only an N2 beachhead question (OEM ESG-data pressure is real, but a common platform is planned for end FY27 and Tier 2/3 come later). Construction and RERA gave nothing for Gujarat. If the owner wants a third hypothesis beside N1/N2: 8-10 personal WhatsApp conversations with recyclers after 1 Nov (PWP return date is 31 Oct 2026).

candidates.niche: Owner-run Gujarat plastic-waste recyclers registered as Plastic Waste Processors (PWPs) on the CPCB EPR portal: audit-ready input, output and invoice records behind their EPR certificates
candidates.geography: Gujarat (662 PWPs per CPCB count reported 7 Jul 2026); clusters not verified
candidates.problem: Certificates are the recycler's revenue lever and can only be generated up to registered capacity and against GST-validated sale invoices. CPCB audits processors (the 2024 fake-certificate case involved two Gujarat firms among four) and in June 2026 told states to act against non-compliant ones. In owner terms: every tonne in and out must tally with weighbridge slips, purchase papers and invoices, or credits stop and compensation or cancellation can follow. How they keep records today is inferred, not observed.
candidates.why_now: MoEFCC notice of 28 Aug 2026 set 31 Oct 2026 for PWP FY2025-26 returns (31 Dec 2026 for producers, importers, brand owners); CPCB told states on 26 Jun 2026 to act against non-compliant PWPs; NGT order of 27 Mar 2026 made Gujarat among nine states to file a reply; PWM Amendment Rules of 31 Mar 2026 changed certificates and audits (secondary sources). The 31 Oct date is 3 days away, so approach after it.
candidates.who_decides: Proprietor or managing partner; the CA or EPR consultant who files portal returns is an influencer (inferred).
candidates.current_spend: Software spend: not observed. Consultants list EPR filing at Rs 9,999 plus Rs 4,999 yearly return per stream (vendor snippet). Money in the system: DTE says one recycled tonne = one certificate at CPCB rates of Rs 870 to 2,500 per tonne; 178.48 lakh tonnes of credits went to producers since inception, about Rs 2,677 crore at Rs 1,500/t (my arithmetic).
candidates.cost_of_problem: Recycler-specific penalty amounts not found. Stakes: right to generate certificates plus compensation. My estimate: a unit doing 3,000 t a year (assumed) at Rs 1,500/t holds about Rs 45 lakh a year of certificate value.
candidates.our_services_that_fit: Custom ERP/inventory module (weighbridge slip import, lot-wise input, output and yield, stock vs registered capacity, GST invoice check, CPCB bulk-upload sheet); AI document processing of slips and invoices; WhatsApp reminders. Reuses the wire-soldering ERP purchase, GRN, production, stock and billing flows (my inference). A reply bot does not fit.
candidates.entry_offer_idea: Free one-page audit-readiness check on the owner's last quarter (tonnes in and out, yield, invoices vs certificates vs registered capacity); paid 7-10 day setup of an in/out/stock register with a CPCB upload sheet. Owner sets the price. No legal assurances; skip units that want to hide capacity breaches.
candidates.sales_cycle_hint: My estimate: 2-4 weeks to a paid check if the owner shares real records; 2-3 months for a module. Nothing found on how recyclers buy software.
candidates.size_hint: 662 Gujarat PWPs (applied vs registered not stated) of 3,079 registered nationally; owner-run share unknown. Adjacent: 741 producers and 109 brand owners in Gujarat.

evidence.claim: MoEFCC notice of 28 Aug 2026 (No. 12/64/2023-HSM Part 1, citing a CPCB letter of 10 Aug 2026) extends FY2025-26 annual returns to 31 Oct 2026 for PWPs and 31 Dec 2026 for producers, importers and brand owners.
evidence.note: Opened. Regtech vendor summary; primary notice not opened; page says nothing on penalties.

evidence.note: Opened. Does not say if 662 is applied or registered, or what Gujarat's reply said.

evidence.note: Opened. Opinion column; no recycler or association quoted; no count of audited recyclers.

candidates.counter_evidence: No recycler or association complaint found; no software spend; no public Gujarat job post found. The enforcement targets fraud (certificates beyond capacity), so exposed units may avoid transparency while honest ones may feel safe. A UPSC-prep summary says the 2026 amendment defers some EPR penalties (unverified). Generic waste ERPs and ERPNext waste apps exist, consultants file returns cheaply, and the CPCB portal has free bulk upload. CSE says about 80 percent of plastic scrap sourcing is informal (The Week, 15 Oct 2025, snippet), so purchase proofs are hard for any tool. The pool includes tiny units (a 10-staff recycler in a directory). NGT report and primary notice not opened.
candidates.reachability: Recycler names, addresses and staff size are on trade directories (enfplastic.com entries updated Nov 2025 and Jan 2026); the CPCB EPR portal lists registered PWPs (contact fields not checked). Owner on WhatsApp is untested.

candidates.niche: Owner-run licensed fertiliser, pesticide and seed dealers (agro centres) in Gujarat that sell subsidised fertiliser through PoS devices and face PoS-versus-physical-stock inspections
candidates.problem: On an inspector's visit the dealer's PoS sales, physical stock, purchase invoices and records must agree; in 2026 so far about one in five inspected firms got a notice and 54 licences were suspended immediately. Inferred, not observed: dealers keep stock in billing software, registers or memory and reconcile by hand. Many actions cite hoarding, overpricing or tagging, which software does not fix.
candidates.why_now: Gujarat Agriculture Minister announced zero tolerance on 10 Jun 2026 (85 vigilance teams, 3,526 inspections, 752 notices, 54 suspensions); on 5 Aug 2026 investigation officers were placed in every district to check dealer PoS records against physical stock, with a daily state control room. Rabi urea demand in the coming months is my inference, not sourced.

V5.summary: Coverage sweep of the six sectors phase 1 skipped. Bottom line: nothing here beats N1 or N2 (22 of 35). Real and visible: salaried manual back-office spend in Gujarat (156 Indeed postings pulled 28 Oct 2026, a capped sample; my count by title: 9 plain billing roles at Rs 9,000-33,000 a month, 11 dispatch, 10 logistics roles up to Rs 60,000, about 20 e-commerce roles, 9 collection roles at non-lender firms averaging about Rs 24,000), plus a few dated rules (e-way bill changes from 1 Aug 2026; RBI TReDS Directions from 23 Jun 2026; CPSE TReDS mandate from 30 Jun 2026). Missing in every sector: a Gujarat owner complaint, a deadline that forces these owners to buy, and a gap that cheap tools do not already fill (AIM Transport from Rs 12,000 a year, Tally and Vyapar reminders, salon software at Rs 800-1,200 a month). Two low-confidence candidates: C2 Gujarat credit-selling firms that already pay a collector (my rubric estimate about 16 of 35) and C1 Gujarat transport and logistics back office, LR-POD-freight billing (about 15 of 35); both are my estimates, not phase-1 scoring. Cross-findings for the ranker: (1) the state ICT refund (65%, max Rs 5 lakh) excludes software and service or trading units (Draft ICT guideline, GR 5 Oct 2022, to 4 Oct 2027) and phase 1 read the ERP line as manufacturing-only, so these sectors have no N2-style subsidy hook; (2) TReDS does not fix Surat trader credit (buyers are companies and CPSEs; neither article mentions small traders) and gives IV nothing to sell; (3) for the N3 gate: HP Telecom India in Surat posted a Rs 25,000-30,000 credit-control job for dealer dues on 24 Oct 2026, the first observed Surat spend on dealer collections, but telecom, not textile, and the Tally and Vyapar counter-evidence stands; (4) for N1: Oct 2026 Gujarat renewable-energy postings (AVI Renewable billing with POD checks, B Safal collections) show back-office hiring spend, but none mentions DISCOM or PM Surya Ghar chasing.

candidates.niche: Owner-run Gujarat transport and logistics service firms (transport companies, booking agents, small 3PL; about 5-50 staff) that run LR, POD and freight billing by hand
candidates.geography: Gujarat (hiring examples from Rajkot and Ahmedabad; also Surat and Vadodara postings in the sample)
candidates.problem: A consignment needs an LR, a valid e-way bill, a signed POD brought back from the driver or consignee, and then a freight bill that the consignor pays only against the POD. Clerks match PODs to LRs and bills across registers, Excel, Tally and WhatsApp photos, so bills go out late and pending PODs hide unpaid freight. Inferred from job duties and vendor feature lists; no transporter was found saying this.
candidates.why_now: Weak. E-way bill changes (Ship-to GSTIN, closure after delivery by transporter or driver via mobile number) take effect 1 Aug 2026 per Taxscan (30 Jun 2026), and a GSTAT order reported 19 Oct 2026 shows an expired e-way bill on a Gujarat-UP trip drew a Rs 1.57 lakh penalty (cancelled). Neither forces a small transporter to buy software.
candidates.who_decides: Owner or partner of the transport firm. Larger firms delegate to a booking manager (Vraj Logistics posts one at Rs 50,000-60,000).
candidates.current_spend: Salaried coordination staff at Rs 15,000-60,000 a month per role in the 10 logistics-titled postings (Oct 2026), plus off-the-shelf transport software from about Rs 12,000 a year (AIM Transport vendor page, undated).
candidates.cost_of_problem: Not measured. The only rupee figure is one cancelled e-way bill penalty of Rs 1,57,516 (GSTAT, 19 Oct 2026); clerical cost equals the salaries above.
candidates.our_services_that_fit: Custom ERP or TMS (LR, trips, freight bills, ledgers), AI document processing (POD photo to LR match), WhatsApp POD capture from drivers, e-way bill API integration.

evidence.claim: E-way bill changes effective 1 Aug 2026: Ship-to GSTIN in bill-to/ship-to cases, URP entry for unregistered consignees, closure after delivery by supplier, recipient, transporter, driver or authorised person via mobile-number access; ERP, GSP and API users must update. The article mentions no penalty.

sector_notes.sector: (1) Wholesale distributors and stockists (FMCG, pharma, hardware, electricals)
sector_notes.finding: No new dated rule: the e-invoicing threshold is still Rs 5 crore since 1 Aug 2023 and a Rs 2 crore cut is only a proposal (compliance-blog search summaries, June 2026, not official, not opened); the state ICT refund excludes software and trading units (Draft ICT guideline, GR 5 Oct 2022). Jobs: Gujarat dealers and makers hire billing and dispatch staff (Kataria Automobiles billing Rs 18,000-25,000, 15 Oct 2026; Kumar Automobiles dispatch Rs 20,000-35,000, 26 Oct 2026) and HP Telecom (Surat) hired a dealer-dues credit controller at Rs 25,000-30,000 (24 Oct 2026). sector_notes.sector: (2) Transporters and logistics operators (e-way bill, FASTag, ULIP, LR and POD, freight billing and collection)
sector_notes.finding: Candidate C1 at low confidence. Rule: e-way bill changes from 1 Aug 2026 (Taxscan, 30 Jun 2026); a Gujarati-language search summary says an earlier 15 Jun 2026 date was extended; a GSTAT order reported 19 Oct 2026 cancelled a Rs 1,57,516 penalty on a Gujarat-UP trip. Jobs: 10 transport or logistics-titled postings in the sample at Rs 15,000-60,000 a month, none with POD in the title; AVI Renewable's billing post shows POD checks are manual work. sector_notes.finding: Jobs: about 20 e-commerce-titled postings in Gujarat (Oct 2026, Rs 9,700-50,000 a month; one asks for Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho and Shopify skills) and dealer back-office hires (Kataria Automobiles billing, Kumar Automobiles dispatch). No dated rule found, and no showroom-specific search beyond job titles. Fails the standard: only one dated kind of evidence (job posts).

sector_notes.sector: (4) Appointment and service businesses (salons, spas, gyms, driving schools, diagnostic labs, retail pharmacies, tour operators, event planners)
sector_notes.finding: Only salons, spas and gyms (one price search) and driving schools (one rules search) were examined; labs, pharmacies, tour operators and event planners got no dedicated search, so 'nothing found' there means not examined. Salon software listings run from about Rs 13 per user per month (JHD e-Salon, Capterra) to Rs 799-1,199 a month (SalonBoost, Salon360, Invoay), and a vendor blog says Fresha is free for solo stylists (search summaries, vendor claims, not opened). Driving schools: MoRTH accredited-centre rules date from 1 Jul 2021 (simulator, test track) with a June 2024 amendment per a secondary blog; no Gujarat, software or 2026 rule found. One tour-operator sales posting (Elite Era Holidays, Rs 15,000-40,000). No Gujarat owner complaint. The price ceiling is roughly ten times below the Rs 10-12K telecaller anchor.

sector_notes.sector: (5) Hiring, attendance, payroll and collection-executive roles across Gujarat SMEs
sector_notes.finding: Method: Indeed India via Apify, 28 Oct 2026, location Gujarat, last 30 days, 9 keyword searches capped at 20 each = 156 unique postings, all with a Gujarat location; counts are floors, not market totals (Apna, Quikr, LinkedIn and job-group posts not run). My count by title: 23 collection, recovery, credit-control or receivables roles (8 lenders or collection agencies, 9 from non-lender firms, 6 unclear or offshore); 9 plain billing executives (Rs 9,000-33,000); 11 dispatch roles; 10 logistics roles; about 20 HR-titled roles and only 1 payroll executive (Globe Ecologistics, Rs 15,000-25,000), so payroll and attendance sit inside general HR hires. Non-lender collectors: HP Telecom (Surat), B Safal Renewable Energy (Ahmedabad), Nestoria Buildcon, Rashmi Engicon (2 postings), VISAMAN GLOBAL SALES, evo innovative Surfaces, SHC Projects, Earth Travel; pay Rs 12,000-45,000, mean of midpoints about Rs 24,000; only HP Telecom and B Safal descriptions were read, the rest is my reading of titles and employer names. Visible spend that feeds C2, but spend is not pain.

sector_notes.sector: (6) Working-capital angles (TReDS invoice discounting, bank and NBFC receivables finance)
sector_notes.finding: RBI's TReDS Directions 2026 took effect 23 Jun 2026 (TaxGuru, 25 Jun 2026, https://taxguru.in/rbi/rbis-treds-master-direction-2026-means-msmes-working-capital.html): platform-level due diligence on MSME sellers removed, platform net worth Rs 25 crore (existing operators by 31 Mar 2028), insurance premium not chargeable to the seller; companies and PSUs are the expected buyers. All CPSEs must route MSME invoice settlements through TReDS from 30 Jun 2026, and the company-buyer threshold was cut from Rs 500 crore to Rs 250 crore in Nov 2024 (Angel One, 10 Jul 2026, https://www.angelone.in/news/market-updates/government-mandates-treds-for-msme-invoice-settlement-by-cpses). Neither article mentions small traders or textile, so Surat trader-to-trader credit is not covered (my inference: most Surat trading firms are far below the turnover threshold). The platforms (RXIL, M1xchange, Invoicemart, C2treds, DTX, named in a search summary) handle onboarding themselves, so in my judgement IV has no service to sell. Bank and NBFC receivables finance was not searched. The money-flow link to the Surat credit pain is weak.

V5.did_not_work: Reddit search through Apify (5 queries, about 120 posts) returned mostly unrelated posts; no first-person Indian transporter, distributor or wholesaler complaint was found, only two builder posts (a distribution CRM, a POS app), so I dropped it. WebSearch is US-centred: 3 searches for Gujarat transporter association demands (one in Gujarati) found nothing from 2026, and no Gujarat distributor complaint turned up beyond the national AICPDF statement. The Indeed sample is Indeed only and capped at 20 per keyword; Apna, Quikr, LinkedIn and job-group posts were not run; the POD executive keyword returned no POD-titled Gujarat role; only 10 of 156 descriptions were read (Vraj, AVI, Techsol, Qlocar, Buck4India, Tropical Solar, B Safal, HP Telecom, MSPIRE, Watchdog), employer type for the rest is my judgement from names, and Indeed posting dates may be refresh dates. Seen only as search summaries and not opened, so not cited as verified: Meesho account-management listings, the Inc42 Meesho seller notice, salon and spa software listings, Gujarat transport-software vendors in Rajkot and Vallabh Vidyanagar, SalesOn, Vyapar and MyBillBook pages, e-invoicing threshold blogs, driving-school rule coverage, the SuperProcure e-way bill blog.
